result.topic_en: Solutions of the one-dimensional heat equation on a half-line with zero initial data and various boundary conditions at x=0 (constant value, time-dependent value via Duhamel's principle, a radiation-type condition, and prescribed flux), expressed via error-function integrals.
result.transcription:
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha\alpha \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}$

$t=t_0 \quad u=0$
$x=0 \quad u=\Pi\frac{1}{2}$
$x=\infty \quad u=0$ $\Big\}$ $u=\int_{\frac{x}{2\alpha\sqrt{t-t_0}}}^{\infty} e^{-yy}\,\partial y = u_{t_0}$

$t=0 \quad u=0$
$x=\infty \quad u=0$
$x=0 \quad u=\Pi\frac{1}{2}\cdot\varphi(t)$ $\Big\}$ $u=\int_0^t u_\tau\,\varphi'(\tau)\,\partial\tau = \int_{\frac{x}{2\alpha\sqrt{t}}}^{\infty} e^{-yy}\,\varphi\left(t-\frac{xx}{4yy\alpha\alpha}\right)\partial y$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} = -\frac{1}{2\alpha}\int_0^t e^{-\frac{xx}{4\alpha\alpha s}}\,\varphi'(t-s)\,\frac{\partial s}{s^{\frac{1}{2}}}$

$t=0 \quad u=0$
$x=\infty \quad u=0$
$x=0 \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}-\nu u+a=0$ $\Big\}$ $\int_0^t \varphi'(t-s)\frac{\partial s}{s^{\frac{1}{2}}} = 2\alpha a - \alpha\nu\,\Pi(-\tfrac{1}{2})\,\varphi t = A\,(\Pi-\tfrac{1}{2})^2 - \beta(\Pi-\tfrac{1}{2})\,\varphi t$
$\varphi t = A\int_0^t e^{\beta\beta(t-z)}\frac{\partial z}{z^{\frac{1}{2}}} + A\frac{\Pi-\frac{1}{2}}{\beta}\left(1-e^{\beta\beta t}\right) = A\left(\frac{\Pi-\frac{1}{2}}{\beta} - \int_t^{\infty} e^{\beta\beta(t-z)}\frac{\partial z}{z^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right)$
$u = A\,\Pi(-\tfrac{1}{2})\left(\int_{\frac{q}{2\sqrt{t}}}^{\infty} e^{-\beta\beta yy}\partial y - [-\ldots-]\, e^{\beta\beta(t+q)}\int_{\frac{q}{2\sqrt{t}}+\sqrt{t}}^{\infty} e^{-\beta\beta yy}\partial y\right)$

$t=0 \quad u=0$
$x=\infty \quad u=0$
$x=0 \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial x} = [-\ldots-]\,(\Pi\tfrac{1}{2})^2$ $\Big\}$ $u = [-\ldots-]\sqrt{t}\int_{\frac{x}{2\alpha\sqrt{t}}}^{\infty} e^{-yy}\sqrt{1-\frac{xx}{4yy\alpha t}}\;\partial y$

methods.what: Solution of heat equation on half-line with constant boundary value (complementary error function)
Duhamel superposition for time-dependent boundary value
Boundary flux expressed as an Abel-type integral
Radiation boundary condition reduced to Abel integral equation and solved
Solution for radiation boundary condition in terms of error-function integrals
